newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia bond yields off highs, correction stalls.
newsitem.headline: Australia bond yields off highs, correction stalls.

text.p: *Australian bond yields were just below their initial highs as the corrective move from this week's 3-1/4 year lows at the long end appeared to stall.
*Treasury offering A$200 million 2020 indexed bonds on Thursday.
Australian bond yields were just below their initial highs as the corrective move from this week's 3-1/4 year lows at the long end appeared to stall.

Disappointment that the Reserve Bank has made no announcement on policy following last week's extremely weak labour force report has been put some pressure on the short end, although bill futures are still pointing to lower cash rates.
Turnover is also relatively slim, which traders said was reflecting the absence of any major local data.
"It looks as if we are entering a quiet period with no key figures for two weeks," one trader added.
September bill futures at around 94.80 are still indicating a cash rate well below current official 5.5 percent interest rates, but have recoiled from the 94.94 peak seen on Monday.
Analysts now believe that if the RBA is going to ease again it was more likely to be around the time of the board meeting on July 1 and the Federal Open Market Committee meeting on July 1 and 2.
At the same time, the central bank would get a further update on the retail sector after the back to back negatives in the retail trade data in March and April.
May Australian retail trade is due on July 2.

The market continued to show a widening bias against the dollar bloc as it consolidated last week's strong outperformance which followed the labour force report. U.S. Treasuries ended a three-day rally on Tuesday despite a benign May CPI, which was largely seen as factored in after Friday's weak PPI.
